title: Tyson Fury Stops Mariusz Wach in Seventh Round, Clears Path to Joshua Showdown
excerpt: The British heavyweight stopped the 46-year-old Polish veteran in Thailand on Friday, keeping the long-awaited Fury-Joshua bout on track for later this year.
body:
• Tyson Fury stopped 46-year-old Mariusz Wach in the seventh round at the Max Muay Thai Stadium in Pattaya, Thailand, on Friday.
  • The fight was not broadcast live on television — it was filmed exclusively for Season 3 of Netflix's At Home with the Furys documentary.
  • Anthony Joshua faces Kristian Prenga in Jeddah on Saturday, with both bouts serving as tune-ups for a Fury-Joshua fight expected later in 2026.
  • India's Nishant Dev features on the Joshua-Prenga undercard in a super-welterweight bout against Cesar Diaz.

Tyson Fury dispatched 46-year-old Mariusz Wach with a seventh-round stoppage at the Max Muay Thai Stadium in Pattaya, Thailand, on Friday, clearing the final hurdle before a long-awaited showdown with Anthony Joshua.

Fury, who weighed in at 18 stone 9 pounds — nearly two stones lighter than his Polish opponent — controlled the fight from the opening bell against a man who has lost seven of his last ten bouts. The outcome was never in serious doubt, according to The Times, which reported Wach "was easily overcome, as expected."

A Warm-Up, Not a Spectacle

The fight was staged without a live television broadcast. Instead, the bout was filmed exclusively for the third season of At Home with the Furys, Fury's Netflix documentary series. Proceeds from the event went to local charities in Pattaya.

It was Fury's second fight since returning from a 16-month retirement in April, when he outpointed Arslanbek Makhmudov at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. The 37-year-old opted for the Wach bout to stay sharp ahead of the Joshua fight.

"I just want to keep sharp and keep going. I had 16 months out of the ring, and I only had 12 months back. So hopefully it's another 12 rounds and we'll go from there."

— Tyson Fury, speaking to iFL TV before the fight

Fury has been characteristically blunt about Joshua's chances. "I think he is a bottlejob. A flapper. A chinless wonder," Fury told The Sun this week, referencing an incident after the Makhmudov fight where Joshua appeared reluctant to engage in a face-off when Saudi boxing chief Turki Alalshikh urged both men to build hype.

Joshua's Turn in Jeddah

The spotlight now shifts to Joshua, who faces Kristian Prenga at the Jeddah Superdome on Saturday night. The Albanian, 35, carries a 20-1 record with all 20 victories coming by knockout, though against limited opposition.

For Joshua, the Prenga fight is as much about emotional recovery as ring rust. He is entering the ring for the first time since a car crash in Nigeria on December 29, 2024, that killed two of his close friends — strength and conditioning coach Sina Ghami and personal trainer Latif Ayodele. Joshua sustained injuries that were not life-threatening but required significant rehabilitation.

"Even talking about it now, it hurts," Joshua told reporters in Jeddah this week. "But I keep my mind occupied. If I stop, you let it sink in, and I'm not ready for it to sink in yet."

Contracts are signed for Fury and Joshua to meet later this year, likely in September, with Joshua pushing for Wembley as the venue. Both fighters will be past their peak — Fury turns 38 next month, Joshua 37 in October — but the bout remains the richest and biggest all-British fight in boxing history.

Indian Interest on the Undercard

India's Nishant Dev, the 2023 World Championship bronze medalist who turned professional last year, features on the Joshua-Prenga undercard in a super-welterweight bout against Cesar Diaz. Dev's presence on a major Saudi Arabian card reflects the growing international footprint of Indian professional boxing.

What's Next

If Joshua handles Prenga without incident on Saturday, expect formal announcements on the Fury-Joshua venue and date within days. The fight would be the culmination of more than a decade of near-misses between Britain's two dominant heavyweights of the past era.
